subject: per cent on axis without using formatter

messages.author: 6e0a397d1d4aab5b
messages.subject: per cent on axis without using formatter
parts:
Dear all,

 

I would like to plot percentages of behaviour. To do so I used the formatter function that I found on Hadley’s website and in the archive of the ggplot group. The thing I don’t understand is if I have stat = "identity" anyway why does ggplot plot proportions instead of the numbers when I remove the formatter? Can anyone help me in getting rid of the % signs next to the numbers please? I would prefer to have it only once in the axis label. (The reason why I prefer % and not “proportion of ..” is because [%] uses less text.)

 

I attached a reproducible example below and also I attached it as an R-script. Besides, I attached the PDF of a preliminary version of the graph. Any general suggestions are of course welcome.

 

Many thanks and best wishes,

 

Martin

 

p.s.: One minor question: Does anybody know how to adjust the gap between lines of text when using “\n”?

 

p.p.s.: Another minor question: If you look at the name of scale_y_continuous you notice that I have added several space characters in order to roughly have both lines centred. Is there a better way of doing it? I’m sure this is not the correct way but without the space characters the second line is anywhere but not in the centre.

 

REPRODUCIBLE EXAMPLE:

 

library(proto)

library(grid)

library(plyr)

library(reshape)

library(digest)

library(ggplot2)

 

# setwd("C:\\Users\\mhk\\Documents\\nur.fueR\\melipona project\\graphs\\")

 

df1 <- data.frame(variable = rep(c("queenless\n", "queenright\n", "queenless\nelected", "queenless\nkilled"), each = 5),

       value = rep(c("walk/rest", "run", "attacked", "hide", "antennate"), 4),

       percent = c(22.45446970, 2.01348485, 31.97083333, 43.48484848, 0.07689394,

             10.16621279, 4.94666667, 42.14618421, 41.41775253, 1.32357855,

             30.16625000, 0.28750000, 3.07625000, 66.43000000, 0.04041667,

             21.89256989, 2.13607258, 34.17805645, 41.71469355, 0.07909946))

 

df1$variable.ord <- factor(df1$variable, levels = c("queenless\nelected", "queenless\nkilled", "queenless\n", "queenright\n"), ordered = T)

 

attach(df1)

 

ggplot(df1, aes(x = variable.ord, y = as.numeric(percent), fill = value)) +

       geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +

       coord_flip() +

       scale_y_continuous(name = "queens' behaviour during first hour \n after introduction [%]         ", formatter = "percent") +

       scale_x_discrete(name = "colony state and queens elected or killed") +

       opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 10, vjust = 0.9),

             axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.52, angle = 90)) +

       opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 11, vjust = -0.25, hjust = 0.71),

             axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.8, vjust = 0.24, angle = 90)) +

       opts(legend.direction = "horizontal", legend.position = c(0.51, 0.97), legend.text = theme_text(size = 10),

             legend.title = theme_blank(), legend.background = theme_rect(colour = 0), legend.key = theme_rect(colour = 0),

             legend.key.size = unit(c(0.6, 0.6), "lines")) +

       opts(plot.margin = unit(c(1.5, 0.3, 0.4, 0.3), "lines")) +

       scale_fill_grey()

 

ggsave("plot.a.2.pdf", width = 90/25.4, height = 90/25.4, family = "Times")

scale_y_continuous(name = "queens' behaviour during first hour \n
after introduction [%]

",breaks=c(0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1),labels=c(0,"20","40","60","80","100"))
does the trick

best,
thomas

Because you used position="fill" which the documentation says is used
to "Stack overlapping objects on top of one another, and *standardise
have equal height*" (emphasis mine). Maybe you want position="stack"

parts:
Servus Thomas!

It is not possible to attach files when you write a message from
Google. Instead, I simply saved the address of the ggplot2 Google
group (ggp...@googlegroups.com) as one of my Yahoo e-mail contacts
and send messages via Yahoo. In this way you can attach anything you
want, just like for any other e-mail. However, when you receive
ggplot2 messages as a daily summary and want to reply to messages I
think one is forced to reply via Google where one cannot make any
attachments. If you receive the messages separately which I don’t
recommend then I think it should be possible to attach files to
replies as well.

Thanks for your help. You did understand me correctly. It really was a
stupid question. I know that I’m an R beginner but sometimes I also
feel like a beginner. I just couldn’t solve the problem, probably
because I haven’t used ggplot for a while and started to forget the
basics. Anyway, following Ista’s advice (position = stack) there was
no need to label the axis twice (I already used stat_identity). If you
have a larger number of breaks and you want to save space in your code
you could also write “breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)”.

By the way, may I ask you where you’re from? My guess is that you’re
from Austria but I could be wrong.

Best wishes,

Martin

parts:
Dear Ista,

Thanks a lot for your help and sorry for my beginner’s questions.
Position stack solved the problem. I could then also remove the
formatter which I only used to actually have the percent instead of
proportions on the axis. The trouble is that I have a lot of work
apart from R and I don’t have the time to use it more often which is
why I seem to forget the bascis :-( plus I’m still an R beginner.
Thanks also for the advice on the line height. That’s a very useful
detail that further improved the graph. Only one thing I did not
understand: What exactly do you mean with “Don't mess with the hjust

setting in opts(axis.title.x. You seem to be going out of your way to
make things difficult. Try starting with the default theme options and

only adjust the ones you need.” How else can I adjust the position of
the axis label? How would you do it without using hjust and vjust if I
don’t want to use grid.text? In my view graphs look nicer if axis
labels are centered and this is very often not the case, at least
after saving it as a PDF.

Best wishes,

Martin

On Fri, Mar 11, 2011 at 7:01 AM, martin_kaercher
<martin_...@yahoo.de> wrote:

> proportions on the axis.
Glad to hear you got it working the way you want.

The trouble is that I have a lot of work
> apart from R and I don’t have the time to use it more often which is
> why I seem to forget the bascis :-( plus I’m still an R beginner.
> Thanks also for the advice on the line height. That’s a very useful
> detail that further improved the graph. Only one thing I did not
> understand: What exactly do you mean with “Don't mess with the hjust
> setting in opts(axis.title.x. You seem to be going out of your way to
> make things difficult. Try starting with the default theme options and
> only adjust the ones you need.” How else can I adjust the position of
> the axis label? How would you do it without using hjust and vjust if I
> don’t want to use grid.text? In my view graphs look nicer if axis
> labels are centered and this is very often not the case, at least
> after saving it as a PDF.

Well sure, use hjust and vjust to change the centering. But you were
originally inserting blank spaces at the end of your axis title, and
also changing the alignment with hjust = 0.71. My point is that the
default actually does center it:

p1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x = variable.ord, y = as.numeric(percent), fill
= value)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +

coord_flip() +
scale_y_continuous(name = "queens' behaviour during first hour
\n after introduction [%]") +
scale_x_discrete(name = "colony state and queens elected or killed") +

opts(legend.direction = "horizontal", legend.position = c(0.51,
0.97), legend.text = theme_text(size = 10),
legend.title = theme_blank(), legend.background =
theme_rect(colour = 0), legend.key = theme_rect(colour = 0),
legend.key.size = unit(c(0.6, 0.6), "lines")) +

scale_fill_grey()


# axis titles are centered by default.
p1

## axis titles are not centered because you messed with the hjust and
vjust settings.
p1 + opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 11, vjust = -0.25, hjust = 0.71),

axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.8, vjust =
0.24, angle = 90))

Now you may want the axis title to be centered within the plotting
area rather than the entire graphic. As far as I know this is hard,
and is something that has bugged me for awhile now. See
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/7f8a51b61af0febb/948e057f9b01971b

So in this case, for a final version of the graphic you can use hjust
by trial and error to get the positioning where you want it. There
should be no need to add extra spaces to the title.

Best,
Ista
